feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: Scientists map key protein interactions linked with profound autism
entry.summary: Research published in the journal Science illuminates a "missing piece" in the biological understanding of profound autism and offers new targets for drug development.

entry.title: Scientists study how the brain of a fish filters out signals
entry.summary: The elephantnose fish is native to Africa and a darling of neuroscientists, for its specialized cerebellum-like brain. Scientists have mapped the neurons in a part of the brain that senses electrical signals in detail, and found that how it filters out electrical noise is more complex than they thought.

entry.title: Kissing apes, anti-splash urinals: This year's Ig Nobels showcase surprising science
entry.summary: The Ig Nobel Prizes were awarded this week for humorous yet thought-provoking research. This year, the ceremony came with a twist.

entry.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
entry.summary: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

entry.title: A N.Y. hospital tried to close its birthing center. This city united to fight back
entry.summary: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, N.Y., took on a national Catholic health system and kept the county's last birthing center open.

entry.title: What's the secret ingredient in these cookies? Plastic
entry.summary: New research at the American Chemical Society meeting showcased a potentially edible cookie made out of — plastic!

entry.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
entry.summary: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

entry.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
entry.summary: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

entry.title: Exclusive: Meet the inaugural winner of Fat Marmot Week
entry.summary: Dawn was crowned fattest marmot by popular vote.

entry.title: 'A glorious dawn launch': NASA's newest space telescope has left the Earth
entry.summary: The tour-bus-sized telescope aims to unravel cosmic mysteries and identify more than 100,000 planets beyond our solar system.
